content.text:
The user wants a taskbar system monitor like the screenshot (this looks like "TrafficMonitor" or similar with RAM/VRAM/temps/network). They want suggestions and questions.

I should ask clarifying questions in a structured way using the question tool. Let me plan a set of questions:

1. Technology stack: C# WPF/.NET (recommended for Windows 10/11 native, easy), C++ Win32 (lightest), Python+PyQt (fast to prototype but heavy).
2. GPU brands support: NVIDIA / AMD / Intel / all.
3. Placement: embedded inside taskbar (true taskbar dock, like TrafficMonitor embedding into taskbar window), or a floating overlay window snapped on top of taskbar, or tray icon tooltip only.
4. Features needed: CPU%+temp, RAM used/total, VRAM used/total+temp, network up/down, disk activity, fan speed, power draw.
5. Design: colors, font, ordering, compact vs detailed, click actions.
6. Extra: auto-start with Windows, settings GUI, themes, DPI scaling, multi-monitor.

I shouldn't overwhelm. Maybe 5-6 questions with multiple choice and region. Since the tool allows multiple questions. Let me ask perhaps 5 questions with options. And also note key technical constraints — Windows 11 taskbar is XAML and embedding is trickier; the safest approach is an overlay window positioned over the taskbar (or AppBar) — ask them which they prefer: "الاندماج الحقيقي جوه الـ taskbar (زي TrafficMonitor)" vs "نافذة عائمة فوق الـtaskbar".

Actually there's a known approach: embed window into taskbar using SetParent(Shell_TrayWnd/ReBarWindow32) works on Win10 mostly and partially Win11 (Win11 22H2+ works with some tricks but unstable). The screenshot looks like TrafficMonitor which embeds into taskbar in Win10, and on Win11 it draws an overlay.

Given user wants both Win10/11, recommend a hybrid: try embedding, fallback to overlay. Or simply a "desktop band"-like overlay positioned on taskbar with auto-hide handling.

Let me ask questions now. I'll include recommendations as first options.

Questions:
1. لغة/تقنية التنفيذ — C# WPF/.NET 8 (موصى به)، C++ Win32، Python.
2. طريقة الظهور في الـtaskbar — نافذة عائمة ملتصقة (overlay) (موصى به للتوافق)، اندماج حقيقي داخل شريط المهام، الاتنين (محاولة دمج مع fallback).
3. بيانات عايزها — CPU, RAM, VRAM, temps, network, disk, GPU fan/power, battery.
4. كروت الشاشة — NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, الكل.
5. إعدادات — واجهة إعدادات GUI كاملة، ملف إعدادات JSON بسيط، بدون إعدادات (hardcoded).
6. هل عايز start مع الويندوز + أيقونة tray.

Also maybe ask about "عدد الشاشات" but can bundle. Let's limit to 6 questions.

I'll ask them, and briefly explain the technical choice trade-offs before/after. Let me make the response short, in Arabic.

I need to be careful: the question tool allows asking; I'll call it.

قبل ما نبدأ، خليني أوضح نقطة تقنية مهمة بسرعة: على **ويندوز 11** شريط المهام مبني بـ XAML ومش بيسمح بالاندماج الحقيقي زي ويندوز 10 (اللي بيشتغل فيه TrafficMonitor بالطريقة الكلاسيكية). عشان كده في أكتر من أسلوب للظهور، وده أهم قرار في المشروع. جاوب على الأسئلة دي وأنا أطلعلك خطة كاملة:

questions.question: إيه التقنية اللي تحب نعمل بيها البرنامج؟

options.label: C# WPF / .NET 8 (موصى به)
options.description: تطوير سريع، دعم ممتاز لـ Win10/11، واجهة إعدادات سهلة، حجم صغير نسبيًا. الأفضل لتطبيق زي ده.

options.label: C++ Win32 خالص
options.description: أخف استهلاكًا للذاكرة وأقرب للـsystem APIs، لكن التطوير أبطأ والواجهة أصعب.

options.label: Python + PyQt
options.description: أسرع في التجربة الأولية لكن حجم كبير واستهلاك RAM أعلى، مش مثالي لتطبيق شغال 24/7.

questions.question: إزاي تحب القراءات تظهر جوه/فوق الـtaskbar؟

options.label: نافذة شفافة ملتصقة فوق الـtaskbar (موصى به)
options.description: شكلها مطابق للصورة، بتشتغل بنفس الشكل على Win10 و11، وبتتحرك تلقائيًا مع الـtaskbar (فوق/تحت/يمين/شمال) وبتختفي مع auto-hide.

options.label: اندماج حقيقي جوه شريط المهام
options.description: الأقرب لـTrafficMonitor على Win10، لكن على Win11 22H2+ غير مستقر وممكن يتكسر مع أي تحديث.

options.label: الاتنين مع fallback
options.description: يحاول يندمج جوه الـtaskbar، ولو فشل يرجع تلقائيًا لنافذة ملتصقة. أكثر تعقيدًا بس أفضل تجربة.

questions.question: إيه القراءات اللي محتاجها في الشاشة؟ (اختار كل اللي تحبه)

options.label: CPU: نسبة + حرارة
options.description: استخدام المعالج وحرارته (الحرارة تحتاج LibreHardwareMonitor).

options.label: RAM: مستخدم/كلي
options.description: زي 9.6/47.9G في الصورة.

options.label: VRAM: مستخدم/كلي + حرارة
options.description: ذاكرة كارت الشاشة وحرارته زي 1.2/12.0G و42°C.

options.label: الشبكة: رفع/تنزيل Mbps
options.description: زي 0.0 Mbps ↑↓ في الصورة.

options.label: القرص: نشاط ومساحة
options.description: نسبة استخدام الديسك والمساحة الحرة.

options.label: بطارية / استهلاك الكهرباء
options.description: مفيد للابتوبات.

questions.question: إيه كارت الشاشة عندك؟ (مهم لقراءة VRAM والحرارة)

options.label: NVIDIA
options.description: نستخدم NVML/NVAPI — أدق قراءات VRAM وحرارة.

options.label: AMD
options.description: نستخدم ADL/ADLX.

options.label: Intel مدمج
options.description: قراءات VRAM محدودة، ممكن نعتمد على WMI/Shared memory.

options.label: مش متأكد / عملني في الكل
options.description: نبني دعم شامل يكتشف الكارت تلقائيًا.

options.label: واجهة إعدادات كاملة GUI (موصى به)
options.description: تختار منها العناصر، الترتيب، الألوان، الخط، ومعدل التحديث، وبتتحفظ تلقائيًا.

options.label: ملف إعدادات JSON بسيط
options.description: أسرع في التنفيذ، لكن التخصيص يدوي.

options.label: بدون إعدادات (ثابت)
options.description: نسخة MVP سريعة، نضيف الإعدادات بعدين.

options.label: تشغيل تلقائي مع ويندوز
options.description: يبدأ مع الـstartup بدون تدخل.

options.label: أيقونة في الـsystem tray
options.description: للإعدادات والخروج وإظهار/إخفاء العرض.

options.label: دعم شاشات متعددة
options.description: يظهر على taskbar الشاشة الأساسية أو كل الشاشات.

options.label: ألوان تحذيرية
options.description: العنصر يتحول أحمر لما يتعدى حد معين (مثلًا RAM > 90%).

content.text:
The user answered. They didn't select tray icon (they picked auto-start, multi-monitor, warning colors). Now I should check the environment: .NET SDK availability. Earlier the dotnet command got interrupted because the shell tried to install Python? Weird — the error mentioned python install. Let me check dotnet properly.

Let me check installed SDKs / runtimes and hardware info (GPU). Then propose a concrete plan and maybe ask a couple of final questions (styling/placement details, "هل عايز أعرض صورة التصميم الأول؟"). But the user said ask until we reach a distinguished plan. I should present the plan and confirm before building.

Let me gather environment info: dotnet --list-sdks, Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController, OS version.

Note: the earlier shell output had a strange error about python signature verification — maybe opencode is installing python for some reason? Anyway, run dotnet directly with full path check.

Let me run parallel shell calls.

Environment: Windows 11 Pro build 26200 (25H2?), .NET 8 runtime only — no SDK listed! `dotnet --list-sdks` returned nothing before "---RUNTIMES---". So SDK is not installed, only runtime. Need to install .NET 8 SDK. Hmm, that could be a hurdle. Alternatively use PowerShell/WPF? No — we chose WPF; need SDK. We can install SDK via winget or dotnet-install script.

Hardware: Intel HD 530 + NVIDIA GTX 960M (laptop, Maxwell), 16 GB RAM, HDD + SSD. No AMD.

Note the user's screenshot shows 47.9G RAM and 12G VRAM — that's the reference image, not their machine.

Key technical considerations:
- Windows 11 build 26200 → taskbar is XAML. Overlay approach.
- Monitor: primary display taskbar. Multi-monitor support selected.
- Temperature reading: GTX 960M via NVML (nvml.dll available with driver). CPU temp — needs LibreHardwareMonitor library (requires admin for some sensors; on many Intel laptops, requires kernel driver for MSR — LibreHardwareMonitor requires admin + driver install for CPU temp). That's a constraint to flag: CPU temp may require running as admin and installing a driver (WinRing0). Alternative: use LibreHardwareMonitorLib (NuGet, MIT) which can read CPU temp via "Core Temp" WMI? On Windows 11 with Secure Boot, WinRing0 driver blocked? LHM's newer versions use its own driver signed. Actually LibreHardwareMonitor dropped WinRing0 because of CVE? They now have PawnIO? Let me think.

As of 2024, LibreHardwareMonitor uses WinRing0 driver which is flagged by many AVs (CVE-2020-14979). In 2025, LHM moved? Actually Microsoft blocked vulnerable drivers list includes WinRing0.sys. Hmm. LHM 0.9.4 still uses WinRing0. Some use "Intel Power Gadget" no longer.

Safe plan: Make CPU temp optional; primary CPU% via PerformanceCounter, temps via LHM if available, with clear fallback showing "N/A" if driver can't load. Also can offer optional "LibreHardwareMonitor bridge" — run LHM in background and read from its WMI namespace. Simpler: use LHM library.

Alternatively use "HWiNFO" shared memory integration, but requires HWiNFO installed.

VRAM: For NVIDIA, NVML gives used/total + temp + fan + power. GTX 960M supports NVML. Good.
For Intel HD 530 — ignore.

Network speed: use NetworkInterface statistics (GetIPv4Statistics / performance counters) or ETW. Simple: NetworkInterface.GetIPStatistics bytes delta per interval. Sum across active adapters.

Disk: performance counters for disk activity, and DriveInfo for free space.

Battery: System.Windows.Forms.PowerStatus or GetSystemPowerStatus.

UI: WPF window: WindowStyle=None, AllowsTransparency=True, ShowInTaskbar=False, Topmost, click-through? Maybe not click-through so settings opens on right-click. Position: compute taskbar rect via Shell_TrayWnd (and secondary monitors via Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd on Win10/Win11). On Win11, the taskbar is "Shell_TrayWnd" still. Position overlay at right side of taskbar left of the tray icons or left of clock. In the screenshot, the readings appear to the left of the keyboard layout/tray area. We can compute the tray rect ("TrayNotifyWnd" or "ClockButton") and place overlay to its left.

DPI awareness: PerMonitorV2.

Auto-hide handling: listen to taskbar position polling every 500ms.

Multi-monitor: get taskbar per monitor and create overlay per monitor (or primary only, configurable).

Settings GUI: a normal WPF window with checkboxes, reorder list, color pickers, refresh interval, thresholds. Save to %AppData%\SysMonitor\settings.json.

Auto-start: registry Run key with --startup flag (or Task Scheduler for admin). If CPU temp needs admin, need to run elevated → auto-start via Task Scheduler with highest privileges.

Warning colors: thresholds per metric with orange/red.

Architecture:
- SysMonitor.App (WPF, .NET 8, x64)
- Core: sensors providers (CPU, RAM, GPU via NVML P/Invoke, Network, Disk, Battery)
- UI: overlay window(s), settings window, tray? they didn't choose tray, but settings access needed: right-click overlay → menu (Settings, Exit). Also need hotkey maybe.

Now, questions remaining? The user asked to keep asking until plan is excellent. I could ask 2-3 final questions:
1. عرض القراءات: عناصر منفصلة (CPU/RAM/VRAM/Net...) بشكل أفقي زي الصورة، ولا "دائرة/بلوك" لكل عنصر؟ Actually reference shows a compact 2-row block. Ask about layout: صفين ثابتين (زي الصورة) أم سطر واحد؟ And size.
2. مكان الظهور بالظبط: قبل أيقونات النظام (يسار الساعة) زي الصورة، أم أقصى يمين/شمال؟
3. هل تقبل تثبيت .NET 8 SDK والاعتماد على مكتبة LibreHardwareMonitor للحرارة (ممكن تحتاج صلاحيات أدمن)؟
4. هل عايز أيقونة tray (ما اخترتهاش) ولا كليك يمين على العرض كفاية؟

Also could ask about language of UI (عربي/إنجليزي) — the readings are numeric + labels RAM/VRAM. Ask UI language.

I'll ask about 4 things: layout/shape, exact position, admin permission for temps, and language. Maybe combine position and layout.

Also I should mention that SDK is missing and I'll install it (needs internet). That's a question too — but I can just do it. Better ask? Installing .NET SDK via winget modifies the machine. I'll ask permission in the same batch.

Let me keep the plan draft concise then ask questions. Actually, better: ask the remaining questions first, then produce the final plan. But user expects progress. I'll present a short technical assessment + draft plan, then the questions.

Let me present:

- الجهاز: Win11 26200, 16GB, GTX 960M + Intel HD 530, HDD+SSD → NVML هتشتغل للحرارة وVRAM.
- ملاحظة: مفيش .NET SDK مثبت (runtime بس) → لازم نثبت SDK 8.
- قيود الحرارة: CPU temp على ويندوز 11 محتاجة درايفر kernel وأدمن → هنعملها optional مع fallback، GPU temp سهلة عبر NVML.

Then questions. Use question tool with 4 questions.

Design details: the reference is a two-row compact panel: arrows + speeds, icons + CPU% (temp), RAM used/total, VRAM used/total. We can replicate exactly and make it configurable.

Let me ask:

Q1: شكل العرض — نسخة مطابقة للصورة (بلوك صفين)، سطر واحد أفقي، أو مرن بالسحب والإفلات في الإعدادات (موصى به؟). Recommend "مرن: صفوف وأعمدة قابلة للترتيب" maybe complex. Recommend matching the image layout with reorder in settings.

Q2: المكان — يسار أيقونات النظام (زي الصورة) / أقصى يمين قبل الساعة / فوق الأيقونات في المنتصف. With multi-monitor selection.

Q3: الحرارة وصلاحيات الأدمن — موافق أشغّله كأدمن عشان حرارة المعالج، ولا نستغنى عن حرارة CPU لو محتاجة أدمن، ولا نسيبها اختيارية.

Q4: لغة الواجهة — عربي، إنجليزي (زي الصورة)، أو الاتنين.

Q5: تثبيت .NET 8 SDK — موافق؟ (ممكن أستخدم winget) + هل تحب نسخة portable exe واحدة ولا installer.

That's 5. Fine.

Then after answers, produce full plan with phases, then implement. Given effort, maybe I should start building after confirmation. Let's ask now.

قبل الخطة النهائية، دي قراءة سريعة لبيئتك:

| العنصر | الحالة |
|---|---|
| النظام | Windows 11 Pro — Build **26200** (يعني taskbar XAML،resolution العارض هو الحل الصح) |
| الرام | 16 GB |
| الكروت | **NVIDIA GTX 960M** + Intel HD 530 → قراءة VRAM والحرارة هتكون عبر **NVML** وممتازة |
| التخزين | SSD 128GB + HDD 1TB |
| .NET | **Runtime 8 موجود، لكن الـSDK مش مثبت** — لازم نثبته عشان نبني المشروع |

نقطتين مهمين لازم تعرفهم:
1. **حرارة المعالج (CPU)** على ويندوز 11 محتاجة قراءة من الـMSR عن طريق درايفر kernel وصلاحيات **Admin** — مفيش طريقة آمنة بدون كده. حرارة كارت الشاشة أسهل بكتير (NVML مباشرة).
2. البرنامج هيكون **WPF شفاف ملتصق فوق الـtaskbar**: يتحرك لوحده مع أي تغيير في مكان الـtaskbar، يختفي مع الـauto-hide، ويدعم DPI والشاشات المتعددة.

باقي عليّا 5 قرارات صغيرة وأقفل الخطة:

options.description: بلوك صفين: سطر للشبكة وسطر للموارد، بنفس ترتيب وألوان الصورة اللي رفعتها، مع إمكانية الترتيب من الإعدادات.
options.label: مطابق للصورة (صفين) (موصى به)

```csharp
public sealed class MetricsService : IDisposable

}
```

# Taskbar Monitor

Live system readings on the Windows taskbar, next to the tray icons:

```
↑ 0.0 Mbps   CPU 42% (68°C)   RAM 6.4/15.8G
↓ 0.0 Mbps   GPU 12% (52°C)   VRAM 1.2/4.0G
```

Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11 (x64). No installation, no background services.

## What it reads

| Reading | Source |
|---|---|
| CPU usage | `GetSystemTimes` deltas |
| CPU temperature / package power | LibreHardwareMonitor (needs administrator) |
| RAM used / total | `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` |
| GPU usage, VRAM, temperature, power | NVIDIA NVML (driver `nvml.dll`) |
| Network upload / download | per-adapter byte counters |
| Disk activity / space | PDH `PhysicalDisk` counters + `DriveInfo` |
| Battery | `GetSystemPowerStatus` |

GPU values need an NVIDIA card. Without one the GPU blocks show `--`; everything
else keeps working. CPU temperature additionally needs the app to run as
administrator; without it the temperature is simply omitted.

## Run

```
TaskbarMonitor.exe             start with the settings window
TaskbarMonitor.exe --silent    start the overlay only
```

Right-click the readings on the taskbar to open settings, pause, toggle Windows
startup, or exit. Running the exe again while it is running opens the settings
window (single instance).

Settings and the log live in `%AppData%\TaskbarMonitor`.

## Settings

- **Blocks** – enable/disable every reading, choose row 1 or 2, reorder it,
  rename its label, show/hide icon, percentage, temperature, power.
- **Appearance** – theme (auto/light/dark), font and size, spacing, background
  opacity, network unit (Mbps or MB/s), custom colors.
- **Position** – all monitors or one monitor, gap from the tray, manual right
  offset, vertical offset. `0` right offset means "just left of the tray icons".
- **Startup** – start with Windows, optionally elevated through a scheduled task
  (Windows then does not ask for permission on every logon).

Values turn amber above 80% and red above 92%. Temperatures turn amber at 85 °C
and red at 95 °C.

## Build

Requires the .NET 8 SDK.

```
dotnet build TaskbarMonitor.csproj -c Release
dotnet publish TaskbarMonitor.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o dist
```

The published folder is portable: copy it anywhere and run `TaskbarMonitor.exe`.

## Notes and limits

- The overlay is a transparent topmost window positioned over the taskbar
  (`Shell_TrayWnd` + `TrayNotifyWnd`), not a real taskbar toolbar. That is what
  keeps it working on the Windows 11 XAML taskbar.
- It hides itself while the taskbar is auto-hidden, and follows taskbar moves and
  DPI changes.
- Vertical taskbars get a floating block beside the taskbar instead of a rotated
  layout.
- CPU temperature depends on the LibreHardwareMonitor kernel driver. If Windows
  blocks the driver, the reading stays hidden; CPU usage still works.
- The settings window always uses the light theme.

NetSpeedTray settings window is on the right. Design characteristics:

So I need to redesign my Settings window (at least the Blocks page, but likely the whole window to match coherently) in that style: left sidebar navigation, grouped cards, toggle switches, footer with Cancel/Save (or keep auto-save + Close?), and a preview.

Important: "بس مش اوى" = similar but not an exact copy. So adopt the design language: sidebar nav, cards, toggle switches, larger spacing, modern look, maybe keep my light theme? NetSpeedTray uses dark theme. My app's settings window is light. Should I switch to a dark sidebar + light content? Or support dark theme matching the app? Hmm.

They want the Blocks page redesigned in that style. The cleanest: restructure the whole settings window into:
- Left sidebar (nav with icons + labels) for Blocks / Appearance / Position / Startup.
- Header in the content area with the page title and subtitle.
- Content: grouped cards. For Blocks: a list where each block is a row inside a card, with name+description on the left, and on the right: an enable ToggleSwitch, a "Row" segmented control (Row 1 / Row 2), up/down buttons. Clicking a row opens the per-block options card below (or an expander). 
- Footer: live preview strip + Reset/Close.

The NetSpeedTray approach uses grouped settings cards. I can implement a modern WPF style with custom ToggleSwitch and card containers.

Scope: This is a UI redesign of the SettingsWindow (XAML + code). Keep behavior identical. Need to be careful not to break the code-behind (control names). I'll rewrite SettingsWindow.xaml and adapt the code-behind where needed (structure of BlocksPanel, details panel, event hooks).

Design decisions (ponytail: minimum that fully delivers):
1. Window chrome: custom? NetSpeedTray uses a standard Windows title bar (dark). I'll keep the native title bar but switch the window to the system dark theme? WPF can't easily do dark native title bar without DWM call. Actually easy: DwmSetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE=20) with 1 → dark title bar. But then the content must be dark too.

Should I make the settings dark? NetSpeedTray is dark. Their app overlay adapts; the settings window could also adapt to the theme. Implementing full dark theming of WPF controls is work (custom templates for ComboBox, Slider, Button, CheckBox, TextBox). A custom ToggleSwitch is needed anyway. ComboBox dark template is significant.

Alternative: light content with a dark left sidebar (like modern apps). This mimics the layout without copying exact colors. "مش أوي" supports not identical. Light content keeps native controls readable with minimal templates. But sliders/combos still look dated (Aero style). To look modern, an accent-colored slider and flat combos would help.

Hmm. The current window already looks "OK" but the Blocks list is a plain list of rows. NetSpeedTray's design is essentially:
- sidebar nav
- page header
- cards with rows
- toggles

I'll implement:
- **Sidebar**: dark (#1F1F23), width 220, nav items with a glyph icon + text, selected item highlighted with a rounded accent bar and lighter background. Footer in sidebar: version label.
- **Content**: light (#F7F8FA) with page title (26px semibold) + subtitle, cards (white, rounded 10, subtle border) with rows separated by 1px lines.
- **Rows**: title + description on the left, control on the right.
- **ToggleSwitch**: custom control built in code or styled CheckBox with a round knob. Implement a reusable `ToggleSwitch : CheckBox` styled in XAML with a template.
- **Segmented control** for Row 1/Row 2: two toggle buttons in a rounded container. Or a simple ComboBox. To match NetSpeedTray (which uses dropdowns), a dropdown is fine, but a segmented control is nicer and clearer. Keep ComboBox for simplicity? The user disliked the block list appearance; a segmented "1 | 2" control looks better.
- **Blocks page**:

  - Toggle switch at the right end.
  - Row selector: two small segmented buttons "1" and "2" with tooltips.
- Keep the list sorted? If we reorder with arrows, rebuilding the list jumps rows; acceptable. Better: keep the list in a fixed order? The order defines columns; up/down changes it. Keep as is.

- The toggle switch: implement a `ToggleSwitch` style for CheckBox:
```xml
<Style x:Key="Switch" TargetType="CheckBox">
  <Setter Property="Template">
    <ControlTemplate TargetType="CheckBox">
      <Grid Width="42" Height="24" Background="Transparent">
        <Border x:Name="Track" CornerRadius="12" Background="#D0D4DA"/>

```
No smooth animation (skip; not needed; could add a simple DoubleAnimation on knob position but complex). A color/text change is enough.

- Segmented control: implement with two RadioButtons styled as buttons? Building a custom control is more code. Use a ComboBox styled? Hmm.

Alternatively use a small `Button` that toggles between Row 1/2 on click (text "Row 1 ↕"). That's one button, clear, minimal: click toggles the row. Label inside: "Row 1" / "Row 2". Use a ToolTip "Click to move to the other line". This is simple and compact. I'll use a flat Button with a chevron glyph.

- Up/down: small icon buttons with "⌃"/"⌄" or "↑"/"↓".

- Cards: Border white with CornerRadius 10, BorderBrush #E6E8EC, margin.

Page layout:
```

Grid: [Sidebar 220] [Content *]
Sidebar (dark #1C1C20, full height):
```

For the Appearance/Position pages, the preview updates live — nice.

- Set `TabControl.TabStripPlacement="Left"` and custom TabItem template to look like sidebar nav. The sidebar background dark requires the TabControl's left strip container styled. This is doable but fiddly (TabControl template includes a border around content).

Simpler and more controllable: use a Grid with a manual sidebar of ToggleButton/RadioButtons and a set of content Grids shown/hidden in code. 4 pages. This avoids heavy TabControl templating and gives exact styling. Implement nav buttons as RadioButtons with a style (or simple Buttons with a selected state managed in code).


```csharp
private FrameworkElement ToggleRow(string label, CheckBox box)
{
    var grid = new Grid { Margin = new Thickness(0, 4, 0, 4) };
    grid.ColumnDefinitions.Add(new ColumnDefinition { Width = new GridLength(1, GridUnitType.Star) });
    grid.ColumnDefinitions.Add(new ColumnDefinition { Width = GridLength.Auto });
    var text = new TextBlock { Text = label, VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center };
    Grid.SetColumn(box, 1);
    grid.Children.Add(text); grid.Children.Add(box);
    return grid;
}
```

Careful: `Background="{StaticResource WindowBg}"` where WindowBg is defined in Window.Resources — StaticResource lookup on the Window's Background happens before resources are parsed? Window.Resources are parsed as part of the window; Background is an attribute on the Window, resolved against the parent scope (application resources), not the window's own resources (which are defined below in XAML but available? StaticResource forward references within the same resource dictionary aren't allowed, but referencing the window's own resources from a property on the window? The Window.Resources dictionary is parsed before other properties? Attribute order in XAML doesn't guarantee but resource lookup from the Window's own property can see its Resources because resources are assigned first? Actually, `Window.Resources` is a property element that appears as a child; the Background attribute is processed during object creation, before children. So `{StaticResource WindowBg}` would fail unless WindowBg is defined in App resources. Avoid: use a literal color for Background, and define the brush resource with the same value.

  `using WinForms = System.Windows.Forms;` and never import them unaliased.
- `System.IO` is a global using, so `Path` resolves to `System.IO.Path`. In UI
  files alias `using Path = System.Windows.Shapes.Path;`.
- x64 only (`GetWindowLongPtrW`, NVML).

## Architecture notes

- `App.xaml.cs`: single instance (`Local\TaskbarMonitor.Instance` plus Show/Exit
  events), the metrics timer and the overlay list. Settings and log live in
  `%AppData%\TaskbarMonitor`.
- `OverlayWindow` is a transparent topmost window positioned in physical pixels
  over `Shell_TrayWnd`, left of `TrayNotifyWnd`. It caches the taskbar handle and
  polls every 500 ms; do not add per-tick `UpdateLayout()`.
- `MeterView` renders one 2-row `Grid`; row-1 and row-2 blocks pair by index, so
  reordering changes which values share a column.
- `SettingsWindow.xaml` control names are referenced directly from the
  code-behind; block rows/options are built in code and rely on the resource keys
  `Switch`, `Card`, `Muted`, `Accent`, `Chip`, `RowHighlight`. Keep both sides in
  sync.
- Settings apply live and auto-save (400 ms debounce). The settings window stays
  light-content with a dark sidebar/title bar on purpose; `Palette` only themes
  the taskbar overlay.
- Sensors: CPU temperature needs administrator (LibreHardwareMonitor driver); GPU
  needs NVIDIA NVML. Unavailable values are `NaN` and are omitted rather than
  zeroed. Optimus GPUs error while asleep, so 0 % GPU is a deliberate fallback.
- Startup is the HKCU Run key, or a scheduled task with `/RL HIGHEST` when
  elevated startup is enabled.
